0.long_answer: Scheuermann disease is a recognized osteochondritis that is characterized by uneven vertebral growth, leading to abnormal curvature of the spine (kyphosis). It typically develops during adolescence when the vertebral end plates do not grow uniformly. This condition, also referred to as juvenile kyphosis or juvenile discogenic disease, results in a prominent thoracic curvature, which can cause pain and postural issues.
